title: Merged verdicts are deterministic (ancestry, squash by patch-id, rebase by patch-id map) and `unknown` is never collapsed into `unmerged`
context: A branch is deletable only if its work is in the default branch. Squash and rebase merges leave no ancestry, so ancestry alone would keep every squash-merged branch forever; a wrong 'merged' would delete unmerged work.
decision: Three methods with evidence: `ancestry` (merge-base --is-ancestor), `squash` (the patch-id of the branch's whole diff since merge-base equals the patch-id of one default-branch commit, from ONE `git log -p | git patch-id --stable` pipeline over the last 2000 commits), `rebase` (every branch commit's patch-id is in that same map). A git failure or unreadable history yields `unknown` / 'search unavailable' — never `unmerged`, never `merged`. upstream_gone is its own signal, not a merged verdict. A merged branch carries the PR number only from the LOCAL merge/squash commit subject, never fetched from a forge.
consequences: Cost is bounded by branch size plus one pass over main's recent history, not by main's history per branch.
A false 'merged' requires an identical diff already in main, so the failure mode is conservative (a stale branch kept), never a deletion.
alternatives_rejected: `git cherry` per branch for rebase detection — its cost grows with the default branch's history for EVERY branch checked (red-team finding); the one-time patch-id map replaces it.
Treating a deleted upstream as merged — a branch can be deleted remotely without merging.
Asking GitHub for PR state — a network call and a credential in a snapshot that must stay offline and deterministic.
